clue.text: A hundred locks for playful ladies

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
locks of hair are tresses

explanation.surface: A hundred curls belonging to some frolicsome women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playful' here means given to playing parts on stage, not frisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who perform in plays on stage are, in this sense, ladies who play.

clue.text: They prompt the player and set the ball rolling

definitions.meaning: lines or signals telling an actor when to speak
sticks used in billiards and snooker to strike the ball

explanation.surface: Something that both reminds an actor of the next line and starts a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre prompt to an actor and the long tapered stick for striking a snooker ball share one word.

clue.text: Lotteries for the bookish burglar

definitions.meaning: draws where tickets win prizes
A. J. ..., gentleman thief of E. W. Hornung's stories

explanation.surface: Ticket draws named after a literary cat burglar.
explanation.walkthrough: Raffles is the gentleman cracksman of E. W. Hornung's novels, 'bookish' because he lives in books.
explanation.definitionFit: Prize draws by ticket share a name with Hornung's fictional cricketing thief.

clue.text: Establishments in which Moby Dick learned his cunning?

definitions.text: Establishments in which Moby Dick learned his cunning?

parts.words: Establishments in which Moby Dick learned his cunning?
parts.note: educational establishments, but whales swim in groups with the same name as places of learning

explanation.surface: Wondering where Melville's white whale got his education.
explanation.walkthrough: Moby Dick is a whale, and a group of whales is named like a place of education.
explanation.definitionFit: Places of learning share a name with groups of fish and whales swimming together.

clue.text: Noble listener on the left

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with one ear turned to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the rank above viscount is a nobleman.

clue.text: Tense prediction by the optimistic prophet

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense, as in 'will have done'
a seer who is hopeful says what is to come will be flawless

explanation.surface: A nervous forecast from a cheerful soothsayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective meaning nervous but is the grammar noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical tense 'will have done' also reads as a hopeful forecast that what is coming will be faultless.

clue.text: Great minds can make him a stepfather to his pupils

indicators.note: make signals the letters of the words are built into something new

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Clever people can turn a man into a stepfather for his students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' rearranges GREAT MINDS CAN; a 'stepfather' here is the father of dance steps, not a parent by marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher of dancing fathers the steps his pupils learn.

clue.text: In Britain it decrees that left is right

definitions.text: In Britain it decrees that left is right

parts.words: In Britain it decrees that left is right
parts.note: the traffic regulation that British drivers keep to the left, so left is the correct side

explanation.surface: A paradoxical British law in which left counts as right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' means correct, not the opposite of left: British traffic keeps to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The traffic code saying which side to drive on makes the left side the correct one in Britain.

clue.text: So Spring is here — let's have a parade!

definitions.meaning: the third month is over, so springtime has arrived
a ceremonial procession of troops past a saluting point

explanation.surface: Celebrating the arrival of spring with a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase as 'the month of March has gone by'.
explanation.definitionFit: A military procession past a reviewing officer also reads as the third month having gone.

clue.text: Deeply occupied in legal writing

definitions.meaning: absorbed, wholly taken up
a deed written out in its final formal hand is so called

explanation.surface: Absorbed in drafting a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbed in something, and also, of a legal deed, written out in large formal script.

clue.text: A spirit in the garden

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Someone sipping liquor among the flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: The lily-like plant grown in gardens is the whole clue, and A plus a spirit spells it.

clue.text: Second-rate weaver's gear may be 11

parts.note: B grade is second class
a loom is the frame a weaver works at

explanation.surface: A cheap weaving frame described as being a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is the answer to 11 across, the arum lily, which may be in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum lily, a flowering plant, can be called a flower.

clue.text: Counterfeit coin as religious image

indicators.note: something counterfeit is faked, so these letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A forged coin passed off as a holy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted holy picture of a saint, venerated in the Orthodox church.

clue.text: Like to speak in order to 0 test metal?

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as gold'
to say is to speak

explanation.surface: Wanting to talk so as to examine some metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The '0' in the clue is a printing stray and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse an ore or alloy to find its purity and content.

clue.text: It gives sound advice to the troops

definitions.text: It gives sound advice to the troops

parts.words: It gives sound advice to the troops
parts.note: an instrument whose calls tell soldiers what to do; 'sound' means made of noise, not wise

explanation.surface: Something that offers wise counsel to soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound advice' suggests sensible counsel; here it is advice given by sound, as in reveille.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass horn sounds the calls that give soldiers their orders.

clue.text: A little credit relaxes wrinkles

parts.note: CR is the short form of credit, a little of the word
eases means relaxes or loosens

explanation.surface: A small loan smooths out someone's frown lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Folds or lines in skin or fabric are wrinkles.

clue.text: Knock-out blow for beauty!

definitions.meaning: a punch that stuns
a strikingly attractive person

explanation.surface: A boxer's finishing punch for a beautiful opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazzling looker, and also a punch that leaves you dazed.

clue.text: Proportional representation to inspire church VIP

parts.note: to elate is to fill with high spirits

explanation.surface: An electoral system lifting the spirits of a senior cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or other high-ranking clergyman is a church dignitary.

clue.text: Tempted when ten dice are shaken

indicators.note: dice that are shaken land in a new order, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A gambler lured in by the rattle of ten dice.
explanation.definitionFit: Lured or drawn on by an attractive prospect.

clue.text: Military files where the. clues are set out

definitions.meaning: lines of soldiers marching one behind another

definitions.text: where the. clues are set out
definitions.meaning: the printed lists of across and down clues in a newspaper

explanation.surface: Lines of soldiers, or the lists in which crossword clues are printed.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop after 'the' is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of troops one behind another, and the vertical blocks of print holding the clues.

clue.text: Pussyfoot provides a slight breeze at sea

definitions.meaning: the foot of a puss, a cat
a light air that ruffles the water's surface

explanation.surface: A tiptoeing person who also brings a light sea breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's foot, and the sailors' name for a light breeze rippling the sea.

clue.text: Often after old Bob, silly!

indicators.note: after means the first piece comes behind the second in the answer, here behind the bob

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated S in old British money
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: An exasperated 'silly!' aimed often at someone called Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bob' was a shilling in pre-1971 British money, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly in the sense of foolish or soft-headed.

clue.text: Condition of the nation

definitions.meaning: the ... of things
a country or political community

explanation.surface: How the country is getting on.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition someone is in, and also a sovereign country or government.

clue.text: A bit of this lesser island

indicators.note: a bit of the words means only part of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: Part of the smaller of two islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island, the poetic short form.

clue.text: Quiet tune for two

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A soft melody written for a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple, a set of two.

clue.text: Old-fashioned military protection post

definitions.meaning: chain armour worn by medieval soldiers
letters delivered

explanation.surface: Armour of old, also the letters delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked chain armour of the past, and letters and parcels delivered.

clue.text: Lacking a handicap does he have the itch to win?

definitions.meaning: a golfer who plays off zero

definitions.text: does he have the itch to win?
definitions.meaning: one who plays with an itch he must claw at

explanation.surface: A top golfer who perhaps itches to win.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a player with no handicap plays 'off scratch'.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer good enough to need no handicap strokes, punningly someone playing while itching.

clue.text: Newly wed healthy in prison

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married
well means in good health

explanation.surface: A bride in fine health who is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a London house of correction whose name came to mean any jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaol, named after the old London house of correction.
